title: Gastric emptying of solid and bread-like meals: curve forms, bread and scintigraphy values, breath-test and energy-dependence evidence (task 5562, LN-3 {R-TRANSIT})
source: Abstracts and pages listed in sources.json under TR-* keys (and IL-ABELL-2008). Several pages returned HTTP 403 or a browser check; where a figure comes from search-result text the Note says relayed. A null Value, Low and High means no opened page gave the figure; rows with Low and High and a null Value are ranges with no central value. Rows marked derived are my arithmetic.
rows: Gastric emptying lag phase, Tc-99m-labelled egg solid, power-exponential fit
24 normal volunteers (dual-labelled meals: Tc-99m solid, In-111-DTPA in water); solid egg
Mean +/- 8 (SD or SEM not labelled on the abstract). Lag = (1/k) ln(beta) in the paper's modified power exponential y(t) = 1 - (1 - exp(-kt))^beta. The abstract gives no k or beta.
Gastric emptying lag phase, chicken-liver solid
Mean +/- 16 (spread not labelled). Lag and half-time rose with solid density.
Mean +/- 14.2 (spread not labelled). After the lag both solids emptied at similar rates, matching the liquid rates (abstract).
Gastric emptying half-time after a whole-wheat bread meal, ultrasound antral area
22 healthy adults (age 24.6 +/- 3.1, BMI 23.1 +/- 2.7); 60.1 g whole-wheat bread, 141.0 kcal, 25 g available carbohydrate; fasting then 15 to 120 min; time zero = start of eating
Geometric mean with 95% CI. Modified Elashoff power exponential fitted per person (mean R2 0.93). T1/2 = -ln(1 - 0.5^(1/beta))/k. The page prints the formula with a typesetting error.
Gastric emptying lag time (ln(beta)/k) after the whole-wheat bread meal
Mean +/- 19.6 SD between people. Defined as the time the curve's second derivative is zero.
Gastric emptying rate constant k of the power exponential, whole-wheat bread
Geometric mean with 95% CI, reported to one significant figure, so beta cannot be recovered from k alone (see the derived row). Oat bread: 0.05 (0.03 to 0.07).
Energy of the whole-wheat bread test portion
60.1 g bread, 25.6 g moisture, 3.1 g fat, 4.1 g protein, 21.4 g starch, 2.4 g fibre
Composition from the paper's table; energy density 2.3 kcal/g.
Gastric emptying half-time after an oat bread meal (5.5 g fibre, 3.6 g beta-glucan)
Same 22 adults; 94.1 g bread, 159.5 kcal, 25 g available carbohydrate
Geometric mean with 95% CI; 17 min slower than wheat bread (p = 0.005). Lag 63.3 +/- 26.1 min (p = 0.010). A fibre-rich bread is a condition effect, not the declared 1270 bread.
Shape parameter beta implied by the reported T_lag and T1/2 (derived)
Solved from mean T_lag 49.1 and T1/2 61.9 min with T_lag = ln(beta)/k and T1/2 = -ln(1 - 0.5^(1/beta))/k; gives k = 0.0337 /min

My arithmetic (level 5), mixing a mean lag with a geometric-mean half-time, so only indicative. Using the printed k = 0.05 instead gives beta 15 (11 to 20 for k 0.045 to 0.055). Moving T_lag by 1 SD (29.5 to 68.7 min) moves beta from 1.7 to above 200: the between-person spread of T_lag cannot be carried as a spread of the parameters.
Median gastric retention at 60 min, low-fat egg-substitute meal with bread and jam, scintigraphy
123 healthy volunteers aged 19 to 73 (60 women), 11 centres; High = 95th percentile

Relayed: the Houston Methodist record was not fetched; the numbers come from search-result text of the abstract. The meal's bread and jam come from the Vasavid page (which names the control database), not this record.
Median gastric retention at 120 min, same meal
Median gastric retention at 240 min, same meal
Relayed, as above. Retention above 10% at 4 h is the delayed-emptying cut-off.
Energy of the consensus standard meal (egg white, two slices white bread, 30 g jam, 120 mL water)
Consensus of the American Neurogastroenterology and Motility Society and the Society of Nuclear Medicine; 72% carbohydrate, 24% protein, 2% fat, 2% fibre
Imaging at 0, 1, 2 and 4 h; time 0 is the first image set immediately after eating. Table 1 did not survive the text copy.
Reported normal gastric retention range at 1 h (consensus appendix)
123 healthy people from 11 institutions (US, Canada, Europe) behind the control values
A range from the appendix text with no central value, so Value is null by design. More than 90% retained at 1 h is delayed; under 30% at 1 h is rapid.
Reported normal gastric retention range at 2 h
Range only; more than 60% at 2 h is delayed.
Reported normal gastric retention range at 4 h
Range only; more than 10% at 4 h is delayed.
Gastric emptying lag time (Couturier formula), steamed rice and egg meal, scintigraphy
189 healthy Thai adults (99 women, age 43 +/- 14), 7 centres; 100 g steamed rice, 65 to 70 g labelled egg with 5 mL oil, 100 mL water, 267 kcal

Median with 5th to 95th percentiles. Lag and T1/2 used only where the fit gave r2 of at least 0.9 (183 of 189). Not bread; a different lag formula (ln(beta)/k - (beta-1)/(k beta)) from the Revheim/Siegel one.
Gastric emptying half-time, rice and egg meal
Median, 5th to 95th percentiles. Women 74 (48 to 115) against men 63 (41 to 96) min; male smokers 56 against non-smokers 67; age, BMI and alcohol had no effect.
Gastric retention at 1 h, rice and egg meal
Gastric retention at 2 h, rice and egg meal
Gastric retention at 3 h, rice and egg meal
Gastric retention at 4 h, rice and egg meal
Gastric emptying half-time of a solid test meal by 13C breath test
90 healthy adults (45 men), age and BMI not different in effect; 13C octanoate or acetate 100 mg in the meal

Median with 25th to 75th percentiles. Breath-test times are not the scintigraphic quantity: the paper's T(lag) is the time of fastest emptying, median 81.5 (65.5 to 102.0) min. The meal's composition is not on the abstract. No effect of age, sex or BMI was found.
Gastric emptying half-time of a fluid test meal by 13C breath test
Difference in T1/2 between hourly scans (1, 2, 3, 4 h) and the full 4 h series
Median difference with 5th to 95th percentiles; concordance correlation 0.993 (95% CI 0.990 to 0.995). Supports reading T1/2 from the hourly points of the standard protocol.
Gastric emptying half-time, 600 mL glucose solution at 0.1 kcal/mL
6 healthy subjects; double-sampling gastric aspiration; four 600 mL meals in random order
Mean +/- 1.2. A liquid, not a solid meal.
Gastric emptying half-time, 600 mL milk protein at 0.7 kcal/mL
Mean +/- 10.0. Pea and whey peptide hydrolysates (0.2 kcal/mL): 16.3 +/- 5.4 and 17.2 +/- 6.1 min.
Correlation of caloric density with emptying half-time

P < 0.05. The abstract gives no regression equation. Early caloric delivery to the duodenum rose with density (46.3 to 113.8 cal/min/kg, r = 0.99), so delivery is not constant across densities in that study.
Energy of fat or carbohydrate that slows emptying equally (4 g fat, 9 g carbohydrate)
33 studies of meals of 50 to 1250 mL, density 0 to 2-3 kcal/mL; volume delivered in 30 min
Abstract paraphrase: initial volume did not set the ml/min rate; denser meals delivered less volume but more energy per minute; no kcal/min value on the page.
Constant energy delivery rate of gastric emptying (kcal/min) for nutrient meals

Value null. Brener 1983 (Europe PMC record: glucose left the stomach at a slow steady caloric rate) gives no number on the page; Hunt 1975 gives none; Calbet 1997 reports per-kg early delivery only (body mass not on the page). A search summary quoted 2.1 kcal/min for dextrose from other papers (not opened), so it is not a Value.
Curve form recommended for gastric emptying data
Several studies with different meals and subjects
Value null (a recommendation, not a number): the abstract recommends trying the power-exponential curve and fitting nonlinear curves by nonlinear least squares. Full text not opened.
Whether solid and liquid constituents of a mixed meal leave the stomach in proportion
Dual-isotope (Tc-solid, In-liquid) study with manometry; healthy volunteers (number not on the text seen)

Value null. Relayed from search-result text, page not opened: the liquid left after a minimal lag while solids stayed in a proximal reservoir, so the two phases are not in proportion during the solid lag. Siegel 1988 (opened abstract): after the lag both emptied at similar rates.
Effect of solid-meal energy content on emptying
Healthy male volunteers; J Nucl Med Technol vol 18 issue 1 page 31
Value null: the page text is the abstract only and has no numbers. It states that increasing solid caloric content delayed emptying of solids and liquids, through a longer lag and a slower rate.
